Prevention: Purchase and use certified seed to reduce the chance of weed contamination.
If farmers use own seed, they should make sure it is clean of weed seeds.
Seeds/burrs can also attach to clothing and shoes - remove burrs when leaving an infested area so as not to spread the weed.
The seeds/burrs can spread considerable distances by streams and floodwaters - use only water from sources free of the weed.
Prevent runoff water from infested land into clean fields by making cutoff drains.
Monitoring: Annually erect broadleaved weed (up to 90 cm high) with round stem which is initially green but turns brown, dichotomous branching with oval shaped leaves.
Check surroundings and fields for infestations and consider direct control when any weeds are found.
Check for flowering and seed development and take measures to prevent seed set, spread and build up of seed bank.
Direct Control (Non-chemical): Any seedlings which emerge in the field should be removed by hand pulling or hoeing.
Cultivate or slash the weed prior to seed set to avoid spreading the weed seed.
Seedbank depletion can be achieved by ploughing to bury existing seeds to a depth of at least 10 cm, followed by the sowing of an appropriate perennial pasture.
A. hispidum lose their viability within eight years so that prevention of seeding will eventually exhaust the soil seedbank and eradicate the weed.
Direct Control (Chemical): Use of chemical herbicides may lead to the development of herbicide resistance.
When using a pesticide, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label, such as dosage
